subject: Redwood privacy addendum & subprocessor questions for pilot
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@starlighthealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@starlighthealth.com, dpo@starlighthealth.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood privacy addendum & subprocessor questions for pilot

Hi Soojin / Vanessa / Irene,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — the team was impressed with the latency profile. We're evaluating a small pilot that would route clinical notes through Redwood inference for NLP extraction. Before we proceed we'd like to get clarity on a few privacy/compliance points so procurement can move forward: 

- BAA: We need confirmation that Redwood will sign a BAA for the pilot (PHI will be in scope). If BAA is only available for Private/on-prem, please confirm.
- Subprocessors: please provide a current subprocessor list and confirm whether any subprocessors have access to unredacted inference payloads.
- Data residency & transfer: pilot will be US-only but procurement flagged potential EU subprocessors. Need to know if any transfers to EU or other regions occur.
- KMS & key custody: does Redwood support customer-managed keys for Private or Dedicated deployments?
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report and a short summary of encryption practices for in-transit and at-rest.

I'm attaching our redline of the DPA (Starlight_DPA_requested_changes.pdf) — can your legal/security team take a look and flag any deal-breakers? Procurement is also asking for a short mutual action plan with timelines so they can move the contract through internal approvals.

Can we get a short call next week (30 minutes) to go over BAA pathing and subprocessor isolation for the pilot? Ideally include a technical person who can walk through network isolation for Private/dedicated options.

Thanks,

Maya Patel
Head of Security Operations
Starlight Health

Attachment: Starlight_DPA_requested_changes.pdf (PDF, 825KB)
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@starlighthealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, procurement@starlighthealth.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood privacy addendum & subprocessor questions for pilot

Maya — thanks for the clear list and the redline. I've looped in Irene from Security and Vanessa from Account to help get you a complete picture. Quick answers up front: 

- BAA: Redwood supports HIPAA/BAA for customers running on Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) and for Dedicated customers with appropriate contractual terms. For hosted/shared deployments we do not execute BAAs. For your pilot (US-only with PHI) Private or Dedicated is the recommended path.

- Subprocessors: we maintain a published subprocessor register; none of our subprocessors have access to unredacted inference payloads for Private deployments when customers enable customer-managed keys and network isolation. We'll share the current register and a short carve-out summary.

- Data residency & transfer: for Private/Dedicated the control plane can be customer-managed and the data path stays in-region. We'll confirm whether any vendor tooling (monitoring/telemetry) that touches metadata is routed through our US-only telemetry endpoints for this engagement.

- KMS/key custody: we support KMS integrations for Dedicated and full customer-managed key support for on-prem packages. We'll outline the options in a short doc.

- Evidence: we'll provide the latest SOC 2 Type II and our encryption whitepaper.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Technical deep-dive (30m) next Tue/Wed with our infra engineer to walk network/KMS options and the subprocessor isolation model.
2) Security to review your redlines and propose tracked changes.
3) We share a mutual action plan and a redline-friendly DPA summary (two-pager).

I've attached a short summary of the DPA items we typically accept as part of an enterprise BAA path (redwood-dpa-summary.pdf). Can you confirm whether Starlight's redline includes any unusual insurance or indemnity asks so we can pull legal in early?

Best,

Soojin Lee
Head of Solutions, Regulated Verticals
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dpa-summary.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@starlighthealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@starlighthealth.com, dpo@starlighthealth.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood privacy addendum & subprocessor questions for pilot

Thanks — helpful. A couple clarifications from procurement and our DPO: 

- Data in scope: the pilot will send de-identified notes initially, but we expect a small percentage of records to contain direct identifiers (MRN, patient name) during mapping. So PHI will be in-scope.
- Insurance/indemnity: procurement flagged that Starlight requires vendor certificate limits aligned with our enterprise policy; I'll attach the procurement checklist separately.
- Transfers: Starlight is US-headquartered, but we have a small analytics team in the EU that may inspect aggregated outputs. We need confirmation that Redwood won't route the raw inference payloads outside the US for this pilot.

We can take the technical deep-dive next Wed at 10am PT — I'll approve on my side if Irene can provide the network/KMS diagram beforehand so procurement can confirm.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement wants a mutual action plan and target dates so we can start the purchase order process.

Maya

Hi Maya — thanks for the detail and for proposing the time. Confirming Wed 10am PT works for us; calendar invite to follow. In the meantime I've attached a simple dataflow diagram and a short checklist to accelerate procurement review (dataflow-diagram-starlight-20270528.png).

A few concrete responses and proposed timeline so procurement can map approvals: 

1) BAA path: Redwood will execute a BAA for Private or Dedicated deployments. For the pilot we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) so that keys, KV cache, and network egress are under customer control. Our legal team will review your redline; if there are standard commercial insurance asks we can usually accommodate with a typical enterprise addendum.

2) Subprocessors & transfers: attached is the current subprocessor register. For Private deployments, raw inference payloads do not traverse external subprocessors when customer-managed keys and VPC peering are enabled. Any telemetry we collect can be scoped to US-only endpoints for this engagement. We'll provide an attestation in writing prior to kickoff.

3) KMS & encryption: we support AWS KMS and HSM-based key custody in our on-prem package. For Dedicated we can bind KMS to the customer's account. We'll produce a short technical note describing key rotation, envelope encryption, and the KV cache lifecycle.

4) Evidence and timing: SOC 2 Type II and encryption whitepaper attached in the drive link. Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
   - Day 0: sign NDA (if needed) and confirm scope
   - Day 3–7: legal redline exchange + security questionnaire
   - Day 8–14: technical deep-dive and KMS/network review
   - Day 15–30: finalize DPA/BAA and procurement PO

Please confirm any hard dates on your end. If procurement requires carrier/insurance specific language we can loop legal.

Thanks — see you Wed.

Irene Choi
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
